worst_places.before: **`eager: true`** — the module is bundled directly into the main chunk instead of being lazily loaded asynchronously. Needed for the host's entry point (it physically has no time to wait for async resolution), but an `eager` module registers into the share scope immediately on execution, before other containers get a chance to negotiate — so `eager` outside the entry point can break the entire negotiation by registering a version too early.
worst_places.after: **`eager: true`** — the module is bundled directly into the main chunk instead of being loaded lazily. There are two ways to keep the host's startup from consuming a shared module before negotiation finishes: the `import('./bootstrap')` async boundary above (the usual choice), or marking that specific dependency `eager` so it ships in the initial bundle and never waits. Use one or the other. Do not mark anything `eager` outside the host's entry point: an eager module registers into the share scope the instant it executes, before other containers get a chance to negotiate, so it can register a version too early and break the whole negotiation.

Каждый контейнер при инициализации регистрирует версии своих shared-модулей в общем объекте — share scope. Дальше, когда код обращается к shared-зависимости (например, `react`), рантайм проходит по share scope по шагам:

1. Есть ли уже версия, совместимая с `requiredVersion` этого консьюмера?
2. Есть и указан `singleton: true` — переиспользуем существующий инстанс, нового сетевого запроса нет.
3. Совместимой нет — контейнер грузит собственную резервную (fallback) копию. Она всегда упакована внутри его бандла ровно на этот случай.

patterns: The zone's dominant sentence shape is a 40-90 word 'fact sandwich': claim — em-dash — nested parenthetical qualification — second em-dash — consequence. It is used for every important idea in all 16 files, so the reader's hardest sentence is always the one carrying the load-bearing point. Mechanically: 269 over-long sentences at 23.0/1k words, peaking at 45.8% of sentences in en/06 and 42.6% in en/07. Breaking each of these into claim / detail / consequence sentences would fix the single biggest readability cost in the zone without touching a fact.

`MFE` is expanded exactly once, in article 01, and then used bare in all seven other files including the question bank — and the same habit applies to CDN, CI/CD, E2E, TTFB, SEO, DOM, BEM, CSSOM, SSI and REST/gRPC. The articles are written as a linear book (they also cross-reference each other as 'article 03', 'статья 06'), but they are read as standalone pages. Every file needs its own first-use expansion.

Russian is a partly-finished translation of the English rather than an independent text: an untranslated `result:` survives in ru/05, `publичит` in ru/03, `не satisfied` twice in ru/03, «одну единственную источник правды» / «одна источник правды» (agreement error tracing 'a single source of truth') in ru/04 and ru/08, plus raw transliterations «блэст-радиус», «лок-степе», «гейтованного feature-флагом», «коллизирует», «неймспейс-незащищённый». Latin words also sit inside Russian syntax as ordinary parts of speech («когда происходит resolution», «cost автономии vs сложности»).

The question bank (article 08) is the structural weak point: 17 answers, 23 over-long paragraphs, 4 theory walls, and zero diagrams or tables even though the seven source articles it summarises all have them. Where article 03 gives the share-scope algorithm as a numbered 5-step list, article 08 flattens it back into a single 140-word prose block; the shared config code block is even reproduced with all of article 03's explanatory comments stripped out. Summarising should not mean removing the scaffolding.
notes:
Overlap with nx-monorepo ch.09-11 is near-total for topic article 03 (host/remote/container, remoteEntry, share scope, singleton/strictVersion/eager, the bootstrap async boundary, 'Invalid hook call') — worth a deliberate split of scope plus cross-links, since neither side references the other.
Two places where the course is the *better* text and the topic reads as vague by comparison: (1) course ch.11 states the deterministic rule 'the first one to load wins' on singleton version drift and quotes the exact console warning; topic 03 Scenario 2 only says the runtime 'may pick a version the remote team never tested against'. (2) course ch.11 reconciles `eager: true` and `import('./bootstrap')` as two alternative cures; topic 03 presents both as required, 60 lines apart (see worst_places entry 6).
Diagnostics differ without explanation: topic 03 recommends `window.__webpack_share_scopes__.default`, course ch.11 recommends `__REACT_DEVTOOLS_GLOBAL_HOOK__.renderers.size`. React versions also differ (topic pins ^18.2.0 throughout, course uses 18.3/^19).
One code-example defect worth a fix pass: the contract test in article 07 uses `render` and `React.ComponentProps` without importing either, and its actual mechanism (the type annotation is the contract check; the runtime `not.toThrow()` is not) is uncommented — a junior will read the assertion as the test.
